sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed two-period panel sampling from \(P\). Population statements distinguish the proceedings paper's Assumptions 1--4 completion class from the strengthened bounded-slope and Lipschitz sensitivity class used for the positive sharp interval.
sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units have observed \(Y_1,Y_2,D_1,D_2\) and one-argument static potential-outcome schedules on the known compact interval \(I\). The simultaneous conditional-parallel-trends clause uses one common full-probability event over all baseline doses, so evaluation at the random baseline is legitimate.
sampling_model.treatment: Baseline and follow-up doses are continuous and exact stayers are excluded. The root sensitivity theorem does not require marginal quasi-stayers. Its completion class adds the \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, and continuity of \(g\); it is not globally equal to or nested with the published Assumptions 1--4 class. Conditional on an observed law satisfying the source assumptions, it is only a restricted slice of source completions.
sampling_model.overlap: Population sensitivity analysis permits arbitrary compact observed support \(H\). Uniform inference fixes a known finite rectangle union \(H\), imposes \(f_0\le f_{XZ}\le f_1\), and requires \(A\ge a_0\). These fixed restrictions rule out support topology approaching failure within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A deterministic rectangle-subordinate cell-mean estimator of \(g\) is combined with the signed empirical measure for \(\nu_P\), Hoeffding bands for \(T\) and \(A\), and a component-respecting finite outer ratio program. The simultaneous event \(\mathcal E_n(P)\) yields uniform outer coverage and the displayed upper rate. A matching lower bound is open for fixed-support sequences with \(R(P)\to0\); support-hole sequences require a new varying-support class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Assumptions 1--4, including marginal quasi-stayers in Assumption 4, Theorem 1 states the weighted WAOSS quasi-stayer-limit formula; the regular witness shows that this singleton is not identified over that published class.
In arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1, Assumption 5 imposes baseline-conditional quasi-stayer support, and Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS.
Without quasi-stayers, bounded conditional average slopes yield sharp intersection bounds in the common-zero-baseline design.
The bounds obtained by solving finite linear programs are sharp under the paper's discrete-support shape restrictions.
The data can estimate an upper bound on the diameter of the identified set.
Identified IV-weighted averages restrict policy-relevant weighted averages of the same marginal treatment effects.
Calibrated projection controls coverage uniformly over a large class of moment-inequality models.
Least-squares series estimators admit uniform rates and confidence bands for conditional-mean functionals.
Boundary-adaptive local-polynomial estimators admit uniform Gaussian approximations and confidence bands.
Finite LP-value estimation is pointwise root-\(n\) consistent under feasibility and finiteness.
Bias correction for slow movers yields point-identified panel limit theory under weak treatment changes.

body.tldr: The marginal quasi-stayer condition in Assumption 4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024) does not identify its weighted WAOSS singleton: at the regular heterogeneous-baseline witness, the published completion class admits an affine recession ray and its WAOSS image is all of \(\mathbb R\). Only this negative result transfers directly to the published class. The positive result is a sharp bounded-slope and Lipschitz sensitivity analysis on a strengthened completion class that additionally imposes the \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, and continuity of \(g\); its attained obstacle interval is not the source-class identified set. Baseline-conditional zero support collapses that interval to the weighted singleton formula in the proceedings theorem, while arXiv:2201.06898v1 Theorem 3 remains only an analogous result for the distinct unweighted target \(\delta_1\). The explicit finite program yields a uniformly honest outer interval on the fixed-support regular subclass. Minimaxity remains open for \(R(P)\to0\) on fixed \(H\); shrinking support holes require a separate varying-support class.

project_justification.gap: The proceedings paper states weighted WAOSS point identification under Assumptions 1--4, but its marginal quasi-stayer condition does not imply the baseline-conditional positivity used immediately before display (4) of its Appendix proof. The regular witness is decisive: over the published completion class, a legal affine recession ray makes the WAOSS image equal to \(\mathbb R\). Thus the published-class singleton fails, and a finite interval cannot be represented as that class's identified set.
project_justification.niche: The class distinction creates the paper's central elbow. The published class remains unbounded at the witness. The positive obstacle geometry instead belongs to a strengthened sensitivity class with continuous \(g\), bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, and the \(K|\Delta D|\) conditional mean-movement bound. On observed laws satisfying the source assumptions this is a restricted slice of the source completions, but there is no unconditional global equality or inclusion between the classes because their maintained conditions and domains differ.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the published-class unbounded-ray counterexample, then gives an exact full-observed-law sharp interval only for the strengthened bounded-slope and Lipschitz sensitivity class. It proves attained interval geometry, point identification exactly when \(R(P)=0\), recovery of the proceedings weighted formula under baseline-conditional support, obstacle clipping, certified finite programs, and uniform outer coverage on a fixed rectangle-support subclass. The common-zero-baseline bounded-slope interval is retained only as prior-art sanity check, and the source's separate parametric estimator is not challenged.

body.related_work: de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024, Assumptions 1--4, Theorem 1, and the Appendix argument immediately before display (4)) state a weighted WAOSS singleton using marginal quasi-stayers, although the proof invokes baseline-conditional positivity. The regular heterogeneous-baseline witness shows more than failure of that proof step: the published completion class admits a legal affine recession ray and its WAOSS image is \(\mathbb R\). This non-representability result, and not the positive finite interval, transfers to the published class. The bounded-slope and Lipschitz sharp interval is a sensitivity repair on a strengthened class adding continuous \(g\), bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, and the \(K|\Delta D|\) conditional mean-movement restriction. There is no global equality or inclusion between this class and the source class; for observed laws satisfying the source assumptions, the sensitivity completions form only a restricted slice. Under baseline-conditional support, the sensitivity interval collapses to the weighted formula in the 2024 proceedings theorem. By contrast, de Chaisemartin et al. (arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1, Assumption 5 and Theorem 3) provide an analogous conditional-support result for the distinct unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\). de Chaisemartin, Ciccia, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Knau (2024, Section 4.2.1, Theorem 4, and Appendix B.2 of arXiv:2405.04465v4) already establish the common-zero-baseline scalar bounded-slope interval, which is used only as an algebraic sanity check. Freyberger and Horowitz (2015), Freyberger (2017), and Mogstad, Santos, and Torgovitsky (2018) inform finite shape-restricted and signed-support optimization. Belloni et al. (2015), Cattaneo et al. (2024), Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), and Voronin (2025) inform the inference ingredients; the proved theorem supplies their uniform composition here. Sasaki and Ura (2025) inform the slow-mover comparison but retain point identification. None of these comparisons supplies the still-open fixed-support minimax lower bound. The proceedings paper's separate parametric estimator is not invalidated by the nonparametric identification counterexample.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The uniform theorem is tied to a fixed known rectangle union, fixed \(\beta\), positive density lower bound, bounded outcomes, denominator separation, and the conservative cell-mean radius. It proves boundary-cell coverage, signed empirical-process control, measurable finite-program endpoints, and ratio propagation on \(\mathcal E_n(P)\), but not minimax optimality. Because \(H\) is fixed and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\), this class cannot encode a support topology approaching failure. The remaining in-class question is a matching lower bound as \(R(P)\to0\) on fixed \(H\); a shrinking-hole transition requires a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.
body.honest_scope: The negative published-class conclusion is exact at the regular witness: under the source's Assumptions 1--4, the completion ray yields every WAOSS value in \(\mathbb R\), so the claimed nonparametric singleton is not identified there. The positive sharp set \(\Theta(P)\) belongs only to the strengthened sensitivity class with the \(K\) mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, and continuous \(g\). No global equality or inclusion with the published class is claimed; on observed laws satisfying the source assumptions, the sensitivity class is merely a restricted slice, and its finite interval does not transfer upward. Baseline-conditional zero support recovers the proceedings paper's weighted singleton formula. Theorem 3 of arXiv:2201.06898v1 remains an analogous conditional-support result for unweighted \(\delta_1\), and the common-zero-baseline bounded-slope interval from arXiv:2405.04465v4 is prior art used only as a sanity check. The source's separate parametric estimator is not invalidated. Uniform outer inference is proved only for the fixed known rectangle-support, fixed-H\"older, bounded-density, bounded-outcome, denominator-separated subclass. Minimaxity is open as \(R(P)\to0\) on fixed \(H\); unknown or varying support, shrinking support holes, adaptive smoothness, vanishing \(A\), carry-over, clustered sampling, bounded counterfactual levels, and optimal interval length are outside the claim.
